title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 113
paragraphs: When the boy was ten years old, something happened to him which made his true identity known. He was playing in the village where the stalls for oxen stood, playing in the road with other boys of his age. And the boys in their game chose as their king this one who was called the son of the herdsman. He assigned some of them to build palaces, others to be spearmen of his guard, one to be the eye of the king, and one to bear messages — appointing a duty to each one. Now one of these boys who was playing with the rest, the son of Artembares, a man of repute among the Medes, did not do what Cyrus had appointed him to do. So Cyrus ordered the other boys to seize him by hand and foot, and when they obeyed his command he dealt with the boy very roughly, scourging him. As soon as he was let go, being all the more angry because he considered he had been treated with indignity, he went down to the city and complained to his father of the treatment he had received from Cyrus — calling him not Cyrus, for this was not yet his name, but the son of the herdsman of Astyages. And Artembares, in the anger of the moment, went at once to Astyages, taking the boy with him, and declared that he had suffered treatment that was unfitting, saying: “O king, by your slave, the son of a herdsman, we have been thus outraged” — and he showed him the shoulders of his son.
